label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: At the end of a book about how the factory worked, here is the rest of what it made
findings.why: A first-build finisher has not been told what the factory or the talk's site is, so the opening assumes the whole book has been read.

findings.quote: The words the agents say are ours, written for this book
findings.why: Who 'ours' is is unclear, and it is the only warning that the speech is invented; it sits in a small italic line a phone reader may skip.

findings.quote: These are the night shift's work.
findings.why: The night shift and ruv-sgit appear with no introduction, so a reader without chapters 1 to 3 does not know who is meant.

findings.quote: The line on the slide matters: the map shows where things sit relative to each other.
findings.why: Telling the reader a line matters ranks their attention, and the next sentence repeats what the slide already says.

findings.quote: You met maps like this one in chapter 8.
findings.why: It points at the book rather than speaking as the editor remembering the moment.

findings.quote: The point is the receipt at the end of each: every decision leaves a record.
findings.why: The agent's line below, 'Allowed, denied, or asked. Never silent.', says the same thing again.

findings.quote: A brief for one part of the argument; several versions made side by side; a review of each;
findings.why: A run of fragments strung with semicolons, then the Studio line repeats the winning idea.

findings.quote: The page of the team's keys you saw in chapter 3, where every key is public and made for one session.
findings.why: A reader meeting keys and vaults for the first time sees something is being withheld but gets no plain reason why.

findings.quote: it may be worth asking an agent to build the next one the same way.
findings.why: This is the only next step offered to someone who has just built a first app, and it is vague: no first action and no sense of what 'one page of your own' means.

findings.quote: The **check** (the team called it the gate)
findings.why: The book switches between check and gate, so a newcomer may think they are two things.

findings.quote: A **handover** is the note one session leaves for the session that takes its place.
findings.why: It leans on 'session', which is defined only a few lines further down, and the list does not link them.

findings.quote: A **Wardley map** is a picture that shows what something depends on
findings.why: The one outside term is explained in the same flat way as the book's own words and is easy to take as team slang.

findings.quote: The difference is the book's point.
findings.why: It tells the reader what to take away, and 'setting' against 'expectation' is the idea a beginner most needs shown with an example.

findings.quote: it reports and does not refuse; it catches mistakes, not a steered agent, as the team's own slide said
findings.why: 'A steered agent' is never explained here, so the cell is opaque to someone without the earlier chapters.

findings.quote: one probably refused or never sent, and none acted
findings.why: The cell is a dense count of attempts with no example, and a reader without a coding background cannot tell what a review step reaching a tool means.

findings.quote: It never says how a control could be got round
findings.why: Reassuring in intent, but 'it' is unclear and the sentence is a careful hedge in the first lines.

what_holds: 91-the-words-used.md: short plain definitions, each with its chapter, so I can look up an unfamiliar word fast.
90-the-tour-at-length.md: one figure, one narrator line and one agent line per stop is a pace a phone reader can follow.
93-appendix-b-the-control-register.md: the setting against expectation split, and the failures listed beside the successes, make it honest about 'how safe was this?'.
notes: Read as a phone reader with five minutes: none of the three sections is a next step after a first build; they are reference material. Only the closing 'Something to try' in section 90 speaks to my situation, and it is thin.
